data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Topical antibiotics often combined: neomycin (aminoglycoside), bacitracin (polypeptide), polymyxin B (cationic cyclic decapeptide)

## Mechanism of action
- Neomycin: 30S ribosome — Gram-negatives and staphylococci
- Bacitracin: blocks cell-wall synthesis (bactoprenol dephosphorylation) — Gram-positives
- Polymyxin B: disrupts Gram-negative outer membrane phospholipids (detergent-like); Pseudomonas

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Minor wounds, abrasions, superficial infections (triple antibiotic ointments)
- Not first choice for impetigo (mupirocin, fusidic acid, ozenoxacin better)

## Dose & formulations
- 1–3 times daily for up to 7 days

## Adverse effects
- Allergic contact dermatitis — neomycin is one of the commonest contact allergens (patch-test series); cross-reacts with framycetin, gentamicin
- Bacitracin: contact allergy and rare anaphylaxis/contact urticaria
- Ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity if absorbed from large wounds

## Contraindications
- Known allergy; large raw areas; perforated ear drum (neomycin)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Small areas acceptable.

## Viva points
- Neomycin — top contact allergen; avoid on stasis eczema/leg ulcers
- Bacitracin — contact allergy and anaphylaxis

_Sources: Khopkar ch.18 (Bacitracin, Polymyxin B); Wolverton 4e ch.41 and ch.56. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
